→ Bash: cd /home/maguire/Documents/chipbag/targets/opentitan; grep -n "tl_intg\|csr_tests\|tl_access\|name:" hw/ip/hmac/dv/hmac_sim_cfg.hjson | head -50; grep -rn "intg_err" hw/dv/tools/dvsim/tests/*.hjson |

I withdrew the finding: all five items turn out to be covered by tests with checks, so none is "planned only". The verdict was accepted. I did not trace whether the scoreboard model fires on the second-round (outer key) condition.

- **fifo_empty items (4 of 5):** The HMAC scoreboard (`hw/ip/hmac/dv/env/hmac_scoreboard.sv`) predicts the interrupt only when the FIFO is empty and was previously full. It clears the "was full" flag on process, start, stop and continue, which suppresses the interrupt. It uses that prediction for `intr_state` reads, which are compared against the design. It also checks the interrupt pin is low at the end of the run. The smoke-based tests enable the interrupt and read `intr_state`.
- **BUS.INTEGRITY item:** `hmac_tl_intg_err` comes from the shared `tl_access_tests.hjson`, which `hmac_sim_cfg.hjson` imports. `hmac_sec_cm_testplan.hjson` maps the countermeasure to that test.
- **Near miss:** `hmac_smoke_vseq.sv` skips the `intr_state` check in some corner cases because the scoreboard and design are one cycle apart. That narrows the checking but doesn't remove it.
- **Gap that remains:** The plan text for `fifo_empty_status_interrupt` is vague. I suggested linking the plan items to the scoreboard checks and listing the suppression conditions.
